t.E578.agn: In 1998 JECFA set a group ADI 'not specified' for glucono delta-lactone and the calcium, magnesium, potassium and sodium salts of gluconic acid. JECFA reported that single doses of glucono delta-lactone above 20 g have a laxative effect in humans and that diarrhoea has been reported in volunteers taking 20–50 g per day. EFSA's re-evaluation in the EU is ongoing (a new call for data was issued in 2023).
t.E578.body: Gluconic acid and its salts are normal intermediates formed in the body during the breakdown of glucose via the pentose phosphate pathway; part of the ingested gluconate is excreted unchanged in urine and the rest is broken down.
t.E578.found.0: In the EU, may be used in many foods at quantum satis (as much as needed)
t.E578.prod: Obtained by neutralising gluconic acid with lime or calcium carbonate.
t.E578.regx.0: Group ADI 'not specified' for glucono delta-lactone and gluconate salts.
t.E578.regx.1: Group I additive; generally authorised at quantum satis (as much as needed).
t.E578.regx.2: Re-evaluation ongoing; a call for data was issued in 2023 (deadline 31.03.2024).
t.E578.summary: The calcium salt of gluconic acid. A firming agent and a source of calcium.
t.E578.what: The calcium salt of gluconic acid, used as an acidity regulator, firming agent and metal-binding agent.
